official_sources: GOV.UK engaging public in new local plans

official_measurement_examples.name: Normal consultation period
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK guidance says formal application consultation normally lasts 21 days, subject to specific statutory exceptions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Publicity method varies
official_measurement_examples.fact: Article 15 minimum publicity differs by application type; site notice, neighbour notice, newspaper and website requirements are not interchangeable.

official_measurement_examples.name: Statutory consultee role
official_measurement_examples.fact: A statutory consultation requirement means the body must be consulted in prescribed circumstances; it does not give the consultee ownership or planning-decision authority.

official_measurement_examples.name: Direction 2026
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 31 March 2026 Consultation Direction adds Secretary of State consultation requirements for specified cases; consultation is not itself call-in or final decision.

official_measurement_examples.name: Representation is not veto
official_measurement_examples.fact: A representation or objection is evidence for the decision-maker and is not automatically a veto.

official_measurement_examples.name: No-consultation cases
official_measurement_examples.fact: Some submissions may have limited or no statutory publicity; visibility on a register does not create a universal consultation right.

official_measurement_examples.name: Reconsultation is case-specific
official_measurement_examples.fact: Changes before decision can require further consultation where the authority considers it necessary; this is not automatic for every amendment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Consultation status does not establish ownership, permission, statutory consent or final development yield.
